project_decision.reason: YOLOv8n achieved the strongest overall detection performance among the three final candidate models. It achieved the highest precision, recall, F1-score and Accuracy Proxy, while maintaining competitive mAP performance. Recall is particularly important for railway animal intrusion detection because missing an animal is more safety-critical than producing an additional false alarm.

evaluation.note: The selected YOLOv8n checkpoint was fine-tuned on the railway animal training dataset and evaluated on the test split. The test results were used as the final performance evidence.

fixed_threshold_evaluation.accuracy_note: Accuracy Proxy = TP / (TP + FP + FN). This is an object-detection metric defined for this project and is not conventional classification accuracy.

selection_criteria.safety_priority: Recall was given high importance because failure to detect an animal near railway tracks is more critical than an additional false positive.

reason: Highest precision among the three final models: 90.02%
Highest recall among the three final models: 85.87%
Strong overall detection performance for the railway animal detection task
final_decision.deployment_role: The YOLOv8n fine-tuned model will be used as the animal detection component in the next stage of the railway intrusion detection pipeline.

next_stage.description: Integrate the selected YOLOv8n animal detector into the railway video-processing pipeline.

caveats: The experiment uses a single seed (seed 0), so confidence intervals and run-to-run variance are not available.
The test set contains 352 images and 467 annotated instances.
Possible source-image overlap across dataset splits was identified by filename; this was not confirmed by image hashing.
Training and inference wall-clock times depend on shared GPU workload.
Accuracy Proxy is project-specific and should not be reported as conventional classification accuracy.
YOLOv10n and YOLO11n were faster than YOLOv8n, but their overall precision, recall, F1 and Accuracy Proxy were lower.
YOLOv8n Experiment 2 was also evaluated but was not selected because its overall fixed-threshold performance was lower than the original YOLOv8n result.
